title: Founders, owners and five chief executives
lede: Titles and dates come from the 10-Ks and 8-Ks unless noted. Anything a source does not support is left out.

people.name: Theodore and Milton Deutschmann
people.text: Opened the first store in Boston, according to the 2020 release from the brand’s owner.[^28]

people.name: Charles Tandy
people.text: Head of Tandy Corporation of Fort Worth, which turned the struggling Boston chain profitable within two years.[^18]

people.name: David Edmondson
people.text: Resigned in February 2006 after it emerged that he had claimed degrees he didn’t hold.[^17]

people.name: Julian Day
people.text: Took over after Edmondson. Company stores fell by 505 in 2006, and about 400 headquarters staff were laid off by email that August.[^10][^22]

people.name: James Gooch
people.text: Joined as an executive in 2006, served as CFO and became president in January 2011 and CEO in May 2011.[^19]

people.name: Joseph Magnacca
people.text: Came from Walgreens. Led the final turnaround attempt, including the 2014 Super Bowl ad, and the company into Chapter 11.[^13][^24][^15]

people.name: Standard General
people.text: Its affiliate General Wireless bought the stores and co-branded many with Sprint, then filed its own Chapter 11 in March 2017.[^21][^26]

people.name: Retail Ecommerce Ventures
people.text: Founded by Alex Mehr and Tai Lopez, REV bought the RadioShack brands in November 2020 to run them online-first.[^28][^29]
people.later: Then: sold the IP in about 70 countries to Unicomer in 2023.[^30][^31]
